answer: Tournament-bracket re-grading resists sybils: contested verdicts escalate through successive independent panels drawn from ever-wider trust regions, and a verdict must survive each bracket round to stand. A copper-ring capturing one panel loses at the next wider draw it cannot reach — the summit of the bracket spans trust regions no single cluster occupies. A colluder's verdict is overturned the moment an uncaptured bracket round re-grades it at the jetty, and the losing graders are slashed, so capturing only the first round buys nothing durable.
